creator: Alexander Terp
description:
`replace()` and `split()` are regex-always while `count()` is literal, so each string function's semantics is a separate thing to memorize. The damage is worst when the pattern is spliced text rather than an author-written pattern: `$1` or `$$` inside relayed prose corrupts the result silently, which puts it in this column rather than in ergonomics.

`split()` is sharper still. It picks regex or literal semantics based on whether the input parses:

```rad
split("a.b", ".")    // ["", "", "", ""]   "." is valid regex
split("a(b", "(")    // ["a", "b"]         "(" isn't, silent literal fallback
```

For a user-supplied separator, the call's semantics get decided at runtime by the shape of the input - the worst case for a find-replace tool whose needle is an argument.

`fr` ended up hand-rolling `escape_regex()` plus `text.split(escape_regex(needle)).join(replacement)`. Three sibling scripts hand-roll the same helper, `fr:26-52` with its reason documented at `fr:49-50`. The script review called this family the smallest cost-to-value ratio in its report, and self-contained with no interaction with existing syntax.

An `escape_regex()` builtin makes the regex-always world livable even if `literal=` kwargs never land, and it's step one for any tool that accepts patterns from its caller.

One thing to confirm while in here: with a fully escaped pattern and no capture groups, `$1` in the replacement empirically survives as literal text, so escaped-pattern `replace()` may already be a sound literal replace. Undocumented either way.

---

### Orientation

- Self-contained builtin addition, docs-first. `docs/funcs/` is the source of truth for the signature, `core/funcs.go` holds the registration, and `rts/` picks the signature up through codegen.
- No grammar or checker work. The checker learns the function from `rts/signatures_gen.go` and `rts/embedded/functions.txt`, both generated - do not hand-edit either.

### Where to start

- Write `docs/funcs/escape_regex.md` to the contract in `docs/funcs/README.md` (required sections in order; the `## Signature` line IS the type-checker's signature, there is no parallel Go definition). `escape_regex(_val: str) -> str` is the obvious shape.
- `make generate`.
- Add `FUNC_ESCAPE_REGEX` to the const block in `core/funcs.go` (the string builtins sit around `core/funcs.go:38-64`) and register the `BuiltInFunc`. `core/funcs.go:536` (`FUNC_UPPER`) is the smallest inline form; `core/func_split.go` is the separate-file form. The implementation is `regexp.QuoteMeta`.
- The split behavior the card describes is at `core/func_split.go:31` `regexSplit`: `regexp.Compile(sep)` and, on error, a silent fall back to `strings.Split` / `strings.SplitN`. `docs/funcs/split.md` documents it ("treated as a regex pattern if valid, otherwise as literal string"), so the runtime-decided semantics is deliberate rather than a defect - which is exactly why an escape helper is the contained fix rather than changing `split()`.
- The `$1`-survives-escaping question is answered by reading `core/func_replace.go`, and the answer is "partly". `replace()` does not use `regexp`'s own `$N` expansion; it calls `ReplaceAllStringFunc` and hand-substitutes `$0`, `$1`, ... via `strings.ReplaceAll` for each submatch. With a fully escaped pattern and no capture groups, `submatches` holds only the whole match, so `$1` does survive as literal text - but `$0` does not, it expands to the whole match. Verified on v0.11.0: `replace("a.b", "\\.", "[$0]")` gives `a[.]b` while `replace("a.b", "\\.", "[$1]")` gives `a[$1]b`. Two further sharp edges fall out of the same loop: with ten or more groups the `$1` pass corrupts `$10`, and each pass rewrites the accumulated result, so a submatch whose own text contains `$2` gets substituted again by a later pass. Escaped-pattern `replace()` is therefore close to a literal replace but is not one. Whatever is decided, write it into `docs/funcs/replace.md`, which today says only that "`_replace` can use regex capture groups like `$1`".

### How to verify

- `make build`, then `./bin/radd script.rad` exercising `escape_regex("a.b")`, `split("a.b", escape_regex("."))`, `split("a(b", escape_regex("("))`, and `replace(s, escape_regex(needle), repl)` with a literal `$1` in `repl`.
- Function snapshots go under `core/testing/snapshots/functions/`. Update with `go test ./core/testing/ -run TestSnapshots -update=functions` (the `=` is required; a bare `-update` swallows `-run`).
- `make generate && make verify-generated`.
- `make all`.

### Done when

- `docs/funcs/escape_regex.md` exists and `make generate` leaves no diff afterward, with `rts/signatures_gen.go`, `rts/embedded_funcs/`, `rts/embedded/functions.txt` and `docs-web/docs/reference/functions.md` all regenerated.
- Snapshot cases cover the full metacharacter set, an already-escaped input, and the empty string.
- `split(x, escape_regex(sep))` and `replace(x, escape_regex(needle), r)` are documented as the literal-semantics idiom, in `docs/funcs/escape_regex.md` and cross-referenced from `split.md` and `replace.md`.
- The `$0` / `$1` / `$10` behavior of `replace()` under an escaped pattern is settled and written into `docs/funcs/replace.md` rather than left as folklore, with snapshot cases pinning it.

### Watch out for

- Generated and never hand-edited: `rts/signatures_gen.go`, `rts/embedded_funcs/`, `rts/embedded/functions.txt`, `docs-web/docs/reference/functions.md`, `core/embedded_docs/`. Edit the sources and run `make generate`.
- Snippets in `docs-web/docs/` are executed by `core/testing/docs_snippets_test.go:102` `TestDocSnippets`, so any example added there has to check clean.
- `regexp.QuoteMeta` escapes for Go's RE2. Rad's regex functions all route through `regexp`, so that is the right dialect - say so in the doc rather than leaving it implied.
title: Add escape_regex()
